title.zh: 失眠食疗方：5种改善睡眠的药膳
title.en: Insomnia Dietary Therapy: 5 Medicinal Recipes for Better Sleep

description.zh: 介绍5种有效的失眠食疗方，通过日常饮食改善睡眠质量，远离失眠困扰
description.en: Five effective dietary therapy recipes for insomnia - improve sleep quality through daily diet

zh.text: 失眠是当代人极为普遍的健康困扰。西医称之为"失眠症"，中医则将其归为"不寐"范畴。在临床上，失眠的表现形式多种多样：有人辗转反侧难以入睡，有人睡眠浅易惊醒，有人凌晨三四点即醒再难入睡，还有人整夜多梦如同"放了一夜电影"。中医认为，失眠并非一个孤立的问题，而是身体内在失衡的外在表现——心神不宁则失眠，肝火扰心则失眠，脾胃不和也卧不安。通过食疗来调理失眠，正是从根源上入手，用日常饮食来恢复身体的平衡。以下是我在临床上常用的5种失眠食疗方，适用于不同类型的失眠。
《黄帝内经·灵枢·邪客篇》指出："卫气不得入于阴，常留于阳。留于阳则阳气满，阳气满则阳跷盛，不得入于阴则阴气虚，故目不瞑。"意思是说，人体的卫气白天行于体表（阳分），夜晚行于体内（阴分），当卫气不能顺利进入阴分时，阳气浮越于外，就会导致失眠。这就是中医"阳不入阴"的失眠病机。从脏腑辨证的角度来看，失眠的原因主要有以下五种。

心血不足、心神失养是失眠最常见的原因之一。心藏神，心血充足则神安，心血亏虚则神不守舍，表现为入睡困难、多梦易醒、心悸健忘。这类患者面色往往偏白，唇舌色淡，容易疲劳。肝火旺盛也是失眠的多发原因，长期精神压力大、情绪急躁的人群最容易出现，表现为烦躁易怒、入睡困难、口苦咽干。脾胃不和导致的失眠在《素问·逆调论》中有明确记载："胃不和则卧不安。"晚餐过饱、消化不良或脾胃虚弱的人，常常因为腹部胀满不适而难以入睡。阴虚火旺多见于更年期女性或长期熬夜者，表现为手心脚心发热、口干咽燥、夜间盗汗。痰热扰心则多见于体型偏胖、喜食油腻之人，表现为胸闷痰多、心烦失眠。

这个方子适合心血不足、心神不宁的失眠患者。百合入心肺二经，能清心安神、润肺止咳；莲子入心脾肾三经，能补脾止泻、益肾固精、养心安神。两者搭配煮粥，是中医传统的安神食养方。在我的门诊中，对于产后失眠、学生考前失眠等血虚心失所养的情况，百合莲子粥配合适当的作息调整，往往能收到不错的效果。需要注意的是，莲子心有清心火的作用，如果失眠伴有心烦明显，建议保留莲子心一起煮；如果脾胃虚寒、容易腹泻，则要去掉莲子心。

zh.title: 百合莲子粥
zh.instructions:
1. 百合、莲子提前浸泡
2. 大米洗净加水煮粥
3. 加入百合、莲子继续煮
4. 煮至粘稠加冰糖调味
5. 每晚睡前1小时食用
6. 连续食用7-10天见效

zh.text: 酸枣仁是中医治疗失眠的要药，在《本草纲目》中被记载为"熟用疗胆虚不得眠，烦渴虚汗"。尤其适合肝血不足、虚烦不眠的患者。这类失眠的典型表现是：人虽然很累很困，但一躺下脑子就开始想各种事情，翻来覆去就是睡不着。酸枣仁味酸，酸能收敛，能将浮越在外的阳气收回来，使"阳入于阴"。需要注意的是一定要用炒酸枣仁，生酸枣仁反而有提神作用。《金匮要略》中的酸枣仁汤是经典名方，这里我推荐一个简化版，方便日常煮制。如果条件允许，还可以加入5克五味子，增强安神效果。一般连用5-7天，睡眠质量会有明显改善。

zh.title: 酸枣仁汤
zh.instructions:
1. 酸枣仁炒熟捣碎
2. 所有材料加水煎煮
3. 煮20分钟后取汁
4. 睡前温服
5. 每日1次，连用5-7天
6. 注意：酸枣仁需炒制后使用

zh.text: 桂圆也叫龙眼肉，《神农本草经》将其列为上品，称其"主五脏邪气，安志，久服强魂聪明"。桂圆红枣茶尤其适合血虚导致的失眠——这类人往往面色萎黄、头晕目眩、心悸怔忡、月经量少。桂圆肉补益心血、安神定志，红枣补气养血，枸杞滋补肝肾。三者搭配泡茶，既能补血又能安神，口味甘甜，很容易坚持。在临床上，我用此方调理过不少更年期失眠的女性患者，她们反馈说喝了这个茶之后，睡眠变得安稳了，白天的精神状态也好转了许多。需要注意的是，桂圆性偏温热，体内有热、口干舌燥、便秘的人不宜多喝。

zh.title: 桂圆红枣茶
zh.instructions:
1. 红枣去核切片
2. 所有材料放入杯中
3. 加沸水冲泡
4. 盖上盖子焖10分钟
5. 代茶饮用，每日1-2次
6. 可反复冲泡至味淡

zh.text: 这个方子专门针对脾胃不和导致的失眠。小米在中医里被称为"安神粮"，因为它色黄入脾，能健脾养胃、安神除烦。山药补脾益肺固肾，平补三焦。红枣补气养血。小米山药粥尤其适合晚餐食用，粥本身容易消化，不会给脾胃增加负担，而小米中的色氨酸在体内可以转化为5-羟色胺，有助于促进睡眠。我在门诊中发现，很多失眠患者都有晚餐不规律或暴饮暴食的习惯。对于这一类患者，我通常的建议是：晚餐在睡前2-3小时完成，以易消化的温热食物为主，小米山药粥就是一个很好的选择。

zh.title: 小米山药粥
zh.instructions:
1. 山药去皮切块
2. 小米洗净加水煮粥
3. 加入山药、红枣
4. 煮至粘稠
5. 每晚食用
6. 小米有安神作用，适合晚餐

zh.text: 银耳百合汤适合阴虚火旺型的失眠患者。这类失眠的典型特征是人到夜间反而精神亢奋，但身体却感觉燥热不适，手心脚心发热，口干咽燥，夜间出汗，舌质红少苔。这其实是身体阴液不足，不能制约阳气，导致虚火上炎扰动心神所致。银耳在《本草纲目》中被记载为"润肺滋阴"之品，被称为"平民燕窝"，滋阴而不滋腻。百合清心安神、润肺止咳。枸杞滋补肝肾、益精明目。三种食材炖汤，滋阴清热、宁心安神，每周食用3-4次，对改善阴虚火旺引起的失眠效果显著。如果条件允许，还可以加入少量麦冬增强滋阴效果。

zh.title: 银耳百合汤
zh.instructions:
1. 银耳提前泡发撕成小朵
2. 百合洗净
3. 加水炖煮1小时
4. 加入枸杞、冰糖
5. 睡前1小时温服
6. 每周3-4次

zh.text: 食疗调理失眠，贵在坚持，一般需要连续食用7-14天才能看到明显效果。除了选择合适的食疗方之外，还需要配合良好的睡眠习惯：睡前1-2小时避免使用手机、电脑等电子设备，因为蓝光会抑制褪黑素的分泌；卧室保持安静、黑暗、凉爽的环境；建立固定的睡前仪式，如热水泡脚、轻柔按摩、听舒缓音乐等。饮食上，晚餐不宜过饱，睡前不宜进食，避免咖啡、浓茶、酒精等刺激性饮品。需要特别强调的是，食疗并非万能。对于长期（超过一个月）或严重的失眠，单纯依靠食疗往往不够，建议及时到正规医院就诊，查明失眠的根本原因，在专业医师指导下进行中西医结合治疗。
温馨提示：食疗方仅供参考，不能替代医疗治疗。长期失眠或严重失眠者应咨询专业医师，找出失眠的根本原因进行针对性治疗。

en.text: Insomnia is one of the most common health concerns in modern life. Western medicine classifies it as 'insomnia disorder,' while TCM categorizes it under 'bu mei' (failure to sleep). In clinical practice, insomnia manifests in diverse ways: some toss and turn unable to fall asleep, others sleep lightly and wake easily, some wake at 3-4 AM unable to return to sleep, and still others dream all night as if watching a continuous film. TCM views insomnia not as an isolated problem but as the outward expression of internal imbalance -- restless spirit causes insomnia, liver fire disturbing the heart causes insomnia, and spleen-stomach disharmony also prevents restful sleep. Dietary therapy addresses these root causes by using daily food to restore the body's equilibrium. Below are five clinically proven dietary recipes I commonly use for different types of insomnia.

The Huangdi Neijing (Lingshu, 'Chapter on Evil Guests') states: 'When defensive Qi cannot enter the Yin at night and remains in the Yang, Yang Qi becomes full and the Yang Heel Vessel becomes overactive. When it cannot enter Yin, Yin Qi becomes deficient, therefore the eyes cannot close.' This means that the body's defensive Qi circulates on the exterior (Yang aspect) during daytime and enters the interior (Yin aspect) at night. When defensive Qi cannot smoothly enter Yin, Yang floats externally, causing insomnia -- the classic TCM pathogenesis of 'Yang failing to enter Yin.' From a pattern-differentiation perspective, insomnia has five main causes.

Heart blood deficiency with spirit malnourishment is one of the most common causes. The heart houses the spirit; when heart blood is sufficient, the spirit rests peacefully; when heart blood is insufficient, the spirit cannot settle, manifesting as difficulty falling asleep, dream-disturbed sleep, easy waking, palpitations, and poor memory. These patients often appear pale with pale lips and tongue and tire easily. Liver fire flaring is another frequent cause, most common among those under chronic stress with irritable temperaments, presenting as agitation, difficulty falling asleep, bitter taste, and dry throat. Spleen-stomach disharmony causing insomnia is recorded in the Suwen: 'When the stomach is not harmonious, sleep is disturbed.' Those who overeat at dinner, have poor digestion, or have weak spleen-stomach find it hard to sleep due to abdominal distension. Yin deficiency with fire flaring is common in menopausal women or chronic late-night workers, presenting as hot palms and soles, dry mouth and throat, and night sweats. Phlegm-heat disturbing the heart is more common in overweight individuals who prefer greasy foods, presenting as chest tightness, excessive phlegm, and restless insomnia.
Recipe 1: Lily Bulb Lotus Seed Porridge

This recipe suits insomnia from heart blood deficiency and restless spirit. Lily bulb enters the heart and lung meridians, clearing heart fire and calming the spirit while moistening the lung. Lotus seeds enter the heart, spleen, and kidney meridians, tonifying the spleen, securing kidney essence, and calming the heart and spirit. Together in porridge, they form a traditional TCM calming food therapy. In my clinic, for postpartum insomnia or exam-related sleeplessness from blood deficiency, lily lotus porridge combined with proper sleep scheduling consistently yields positive results. Note: lotus seed heart (the green germ) has a stronger heart-clearing effect. If insomnia is accompanied by significant irritability, keep the germ in; if you have a cold spleen-stomach with tendency to diarrhea, remove it.

en.title: Lily Lotus Porridge
en.instructions:
1. Soak lily bulb and lotus seed
2. Wash rice, add water to make porridge
3. Add lily and lotus, continue cooking
4. Add rock sugar when thick
5. Eat 1 hour before bed
6. Continue 7-10 days for effect

en.text: Suanzaoren (sour jujube kernel) is the foremost herb for insomnia in TCM. The Bencao Gangmu records that 'roasted Suanzaoren treats deficiency-related insomnia, irritability, thirst, and deficient sweating.' It is especially suited for liver blood deficiency with deficiency-type restlessness. The hallmark presentation: the person feels exhausted and sleepy but as soon as they lie down, their mind races with thoughts, tossing and turning unable to sleep. Suanzaoren's sour flavor astringes and gathers floating Yang back into Yin. Crucially, the kernel must be roasted before use -- raw Suanzaoren actually has a stimulating effect. The classic formula Suanzaoren Tang from Jingui Yaolue is well-known; here I recommend a simplified version for home preparation. If available, add 5g of Schisandra fruit to enhance the calming effect. Consistent use for 5-7 days typically brings significant sleep improvement.

en.title: Suanzaoren Soup
en.instructions:
1. Fry and crush sour jujube kernel
2. Add all ingredients, decoct
3. Boil 20 minutes, extract liquid
4. Drink warm before bed
5. Once daily, use 5-7 days
6. Note: Sour jujube kernel must be fried before use

en.text: Longan (dragon eye fruit) is classified as a top-grade herb in the Shennong Bencao Jing, which states it 'treats the five organ evil Qi, calms the mind, and with prolonged use strengthens the soul and sharpens intelligence.' Longan red date tea is especially suited for blood-deficiency insomnia -- patients with sallow complexion, dizziness, palpitations, and scanty menstruation. Longan flesh tonifies heart blood and calms the spirit, red dates tonify Qi and nourish blood, and goji berries nourish the liver and kidney. Together as a tea, it is sweet-tasting and easy to maintain regularly. I have used this formula for many menopausal women with insomnia; they report more settled sleep and improved daytime energy. Note that longan is warm in nature; those with internal heat, dry mouth, or constipation should avoid overconsumption.

en.title: Longan Red Date Tea
en.instructions:
1. Remove date seeds, slice
2. Place all in cup
3. Add boiling water
4. Cover and steep 10 minutes
5. Drink as tea, 1-2 times daily
6. Can re-steep until flavor fades

en.text: This recipe specifically targets insomnia from spleen-stomach disharmony. Millet is called 'the calming grain' in TCM because its yellow color enters the spleen, strengthening it and calming the spirit. Chinese yam tonifies the spleen, lung, and kidney -- gently nourishing all three burners. Red dates tonify Qi and blood. Millet yam porridge is ideal for dinner as it is easily digested without burdening the stomach, while millet's tryptophan content converts to serotonin in the body, aiding sleep. In my clinic, many insomnia patients have irregular dinner habits or tend to overeat. My standard advice: finish dinner 2-3 hours before bedtime, focus on easily digestible warm foods, and millet yam porridge is an excellent choice.

en.title: Millet Yam Porridge
en.instructions:
1. Peel yam, cut into chunks
2. Wash millet, add water for porridge
3. Add yam and dates
4. Cook until thick
5. Eat every evening
6. Millet calms spirit, ideal for dinner

en.text: Tremella lily soup suits Yin-deficiency-with-fire insomnia. The hallmark presentation: the person feels paradoxically alert at night despite bodily heat, with hot palms and soles, dry mouth and throat, night sweats, and a red tongue with scant coating. This results from insufficient Yin fluids failing to restrain Yang, causing deficient fire to flare upward and disturb the spirit. Tremella (white fungus) is recorded in the Bencao Gangmu as 'moistening the lung and nourishing Yin,' earning it the name 'commoner's bird's nest' for its nourishing yet non-cloying properties. Lily bulb clears heart fire and calms the spirit. Goji berries nourish the liver and kidney. Simmered together, this soup nourishes Yin, clears heat, and calms the spirit. Consumed 3-4 times weekly, it is remarkably effective for improving Yin-deficiency insomnia. If available, add a small amount of Ophiopogon (Maidong) to enhance the Yin-nourishing effect.

en.title: Tremella Lily Soup
en.instructions:
1. Soak tremella, tear into pieces
2. Wash lily bulb
3. Simmer for 1 hour
4. Add goji and sugar
5. Drink warm 1 hour before bed
6. 3-4 times weekly

en.text: Dietary therapy for insomnia requires consistency -- typically 7-14 days of regular consumption before noticeable improvement appears. Alongside the appropriate dietary recipe, good sleep hygiene is essential: avoid electronic devices (phones, computers) 1-2 hours before bed as blue light suppresses melatonin production; keep the bedroom dark, quiet, and cool; establish a relaxing bedtime ritual such as warm foot baths, gentle massage, or soothing music. Dietarily, avoid heavy dinners, eating before bed, and stimulants like coffee, strong tea, and alcohol. It must be emphasized that dietary therapy is not a panacea. For chronic (over one month) or severe insomnia, dietary approaches alone are often insufficient. Seek proper medical evaluation to identify the root cause and receive integrated TCM-Western medical treatment under professional supervision.
Note: Recipes are for reference only, not replacing medical treatment. Those with long-term or severe insomnia should consult a physician to identify root causes for targeted treatment.
